environment: Node 24, python3, git on macOS APFS, scratch repos from cli-runner, no network

cases.title: Branches of S-002, S-0010, S-001a, S-0001, run, verify, user, feature and odd attempt-like
cases.given: scratch git repo with the branches named in the test
cases.when: run branches.py list --repo . --kind attempt, keep entries whose id equals S-001 ignoring case, run git branch -D per entry (argv, no shell)
cases.then: Branches of S-002, S-0010, S-001a, S-0001, run, verify, user, feature and odd attempt-like names survive; only the two S-001 attempt branches go
cases.specSource: R-093 acceptance; plan S-027b step 4 'never any other branch'

attacks.charter: Explore case folding of the id filter
attacks.input: Branch sdlc/ſ-001-attempt-1 (U+017F), filter by upper-casing instead of lower-casing
attacks.observed: upper-casing folds it onto S-001 and would delete it; the prompt says ignoring case and lower-casing does not match. On macOS APFS git itself cannot hold both sdlc/ſ-001 and sdlc/S-001 branches

seeds.title: Integrator step 2 says 'ignoring case' without naming a method
seeds.detail: A literal reader who upper-cases or casefolds the id would match a branch named with U+017F (long s) as S-001. Lower-casing is safe. Naming 'lower-case both sides' would remove the doubt. Needs a branch name an attacker already made in the repo, so it is outside the threat model.
